newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat sees break-up blocked, counts cost.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat sees break-up blocked, counts cost.

text.p: British property company Greycoat Plc said on Thursday that its extraordinary general meeting was likely to vote down a break-up proposal forced before the meeting by rebel shareholders.

Although a detailed poll called at the meeting was not due to be completed until later in the afternoon, the company was confident that, after the withdrawal of the proposal's main backers UK Active Value Advisers Ltd (UKAV) yesterday, shareholders were unlikely to back the move.
Based on an initial vote of proxies, holders of 35.17 million shares rejected the move and 4.06 million backed it.

Company chairman Michael Beckett told the meeting that the resolution, which led to first an adjourned egm and then today's gathering, had cost around 300,000 stg to deal with, equivalent to a 20 percent increase in the company's dividend.
"Even more significantly, it has been an enormous and costly diversion of managment time and effort", he said.
The resolution had called on the board "to be instructed forthwith to seek purchasers for all the company's assets".
